correctness.rationale: For λ>2 the Dirichlet path transfer has no poles, and its two endpoint-to-first-interior coefficients are U_(ℓ−2)/U_(ℓ−1) and 1/U_(ℓ−1), evaluated at λ/2. Inserting them at each degree-d junction gives the stated scalar map on the exact parent eigenspaces with equal multiplicities; an eigenvector vanishing on all junctions is zero. After λ=u+1/u, the transformed equation in RESULT.md lines 60–66 has derivative 2ρ+O_d(ℓρ^(−ℓ)) on |u−ρ|≤C_dρ^(−ℓ). The term −μ(u²−1)u^(−ℓ) is uniformly bounded for μ∈[−d,d], and choosing C_d sufficiently large brackets its perturbation of the simple root. Taylor expansion yields shift μ(d−2)ρ^(−ℓ)/(2ρ)+O_d(ℓρ^(−2ℓ)); multiplying by the derivative 1−ρ^(−2) gives the claimed c_d. Interlacing at the Dirichlet principal block gives at most n eigenvalues above 2, and the eigenspace extensions attain that count. Even for a non-spectral μ in the interval, the secular quotient λ−(dU_(ℓ−2)+μ)/U_(ℓ−1) is strictly increasing: the rational term is a nonnegative combination with weights (d±μ)/2 of the symmetric and antisymmetric endpoint resolvent forms, each nonincreasing above 2. This also rules out additional scalar roots for the continuum extension. The implicit μ derivative is positive, so the width is the difference of the two endpoint eigenvalues; μ_min=−d iff the connected parent is bipartite. All constants use only d and neither the maximum multiplicity nor parent order. The frozen verify.py, requirements and VERIFICATION.md document finite checks, inspected rather than executed. The proof is for the above-2 band, not the entire enlarged spectrum.

value.rationale: The common limiting junction energy loses all information about the parent spectrum. Resolving the first-order band with control independent of network order restores every parent eigenvalue at a specified resolution, and distinguishes bipartite and nonbipartite parents by the sharp degree-controlled bandwidth. Uniformity is useful when varying topology and size at fixed degree, beyond merely recalculating a junction energy or a single finite graph.
